assessments.reasoning: The six controlled ranges in the pinned SPDX artifact identify the 3.29.0 creator and the ListedLicense identifier, name, deprecation flag, example header and explanation. The comment directly answers whether filled or empty feature lists affect the generic choice. The example demonstrates where a work notice would record those details.

challenge.method: Tested whether the example's list placeholders require populated lists or exclude known absences. Compared a 1.1-only grant with zero Invariant Sections and a Back-Cover Text, a 1.1-only grant with all three features absent, an unavailable notice with no other authorization evidence, and an express or-later grant.
challenge.results: The generic identifier can describe the edition choice in both 1.1-only cases. In the first it leaves the known Back-Cover Text unexpressed. In the second it leaves all three known absences unexpressed. The unavailable notice cannot establish 1.1-only authorization. The or-later grant permits a broader choice, which the generic edition-only identifier would misstate.

limitations: The finding concerns revision 1 and SPDX License List 3.29.0 at 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48.

The comment puts only before the feature qualifier in its optional-feature references. In particular, its GFDL-1.1-only-no-invariants spelling conflicts with the separately acquired feature-specific filename and spdxId. The generic identifier itself is consistent across its filename, spdxId and comment.
The generic identifier records an established edition choice. Its feature neutrality cannot supply missing evidence of a work's authorization.
reasoning: The ListedLicense spdxId is http://spdx.org/licenses/GFDL-1.1-only. Its final component matches GFDL-1.1-only.json. The name is GNU Free Documentation License v1.1 only, and expandedlicensing_isDeprecatedLicenseId is false. Its example header selects 1.1 and has separate list placeholders for Invariant Sections, Front-Cover Texts and Back-Cover Texts. The comment explains that the identifier leaves each feature unspecified. This applies even when the actual feature facts are known.
